case_name: U.P. Raghavendra Acharya and Others v State of Karnataka and Others
facts: The appellants are retired teachers of University and Private Aided Colleges.
They have retired during the period 1.1.1996 to 31.3.1998.
The Government of Karnataka extended the UGC pay scales as revised from 1.1.1996, inter alia to the teachers of Government and Aided Colleges.
A notification was issued by the Government of India on 22.7.2000, extending the UGC pay scales from 1.1.1996, to the teachers, librarians, etc. of the Government/Aided Colleges.

The mode of payment of arrears in the revised scales of pay was to be made as under: The arrears of pay and allowances during the period from 1.1.1996 to 31.5.1999 shall be invested in the NSC VIII issue in multiples of Rs.100 to the extent of 80% of the amount, the balance amount being paid in cash.
Writ petitions were filed before the Karnataka High Court questioning the said notifications dated 22.7.2000 and 8.8.2000.
issues: Whether the revised scales of pay became applicable in respect of those teachers who had retired during the period from 1.1.1996 to 31.3.1998.
Whether the impugned notifications were illegal.
court_reasoning: The learned Single Judge in his judgment opined that in view of the notification dated 22.7.1999, issued by the State of Karnataka, the revised scales of pay became applicable in respect of those teachers who had retired during the period from 1.1.1996 to 31.3.1998 and they could not have been deprived of the said benefit.
holding: The revised scales of pay became applicable in respect of those teachers who had retired during the period from 1.1.1996 to 31.3.1998.
